cx2_truthful.basis: SR-3051 authorized Varga’s work on MS-6A inside R-6. Ticket and parts records support the walk tests, failed detector diagnosis, and subsequent work at WB-2. Alarms before entry and after departure support detector malfunction as the explanation for later motion events. AP-6C recorded no opening. The records close the main gaps without establishing concealed involvement.

cx2_deceptive.basis: SR-3051 covered an outside door contact and was closed before entry; it did not authorize R-6 entry or panel work. Badge and tamper records corroborate Varga’s admitted panel opening. Despite acknowledging the ticket’s scope and panel activity, Varga omits the entry’s purpose and a full walkthrough, avoiding an explanation of the established activity outside the assigned task.

cx3.basis: The assigned ticket’s named device is unknown, leaving authorization for R-6 entry unresolved. A1–A2 describe detector testing, a failing head, and departure around 21:25. Later motion does not establish Varga’s continued presence, and its cause remains unresolved. The available records neither establish involvement concealed by the answers nor close the main gaps.
